description: A puzzle with no instructions except the one on the panel: three lights have to be made green, and working out how is the module

params.text: One of three numbered knobs whose settings have to be guessed; the first light comes on when any one of them is right and the second when all three are
Sets the whole volts of a number the module is holding in secret, 0 to 10
Adds a fraction of a volt to the larger knob's setting, 0 to 1, so the two together can be matched against the hidden number to three decimal places

inputs.text: Meets a condition while the voltage here is exactly the two output voltages added together
Meets a condition while the voltage here is exactly the one the red output is carrying
Meets a condition while the voltage here is exactly the negative of the one the green output is carrying

outputs.text: Carries a random voltage between 0V and 1V that is redrawn every 2000 samples, but only once the first light is on
Carries a second random voltage between 0V and 1V, redrawn at the same instants, but only once the second light is on
Counts the conditions met so far, one volt for each, until all five are met; from then on it carries the hidden number the two lower knobs have to be matched to

notes: the three coloured input jacks are meant to be fed from the module's own coloured outputs: the test is for exact equality against a voltage redrawn every 2000 samples, which no knob can meet.
the third light needs the two lower knobs held on the hidden number many times over; the score built up by holding a match drains away by one count per sample between matches.
the module's source code gives the knob settings away, and a comment in it says that reading them spoils the puzzle.

inputs.0:
0 to 2V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
0 to 1V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
-1 to 0V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
